@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
++++
+title = "Waterjet cutting"
+description = "The Waterjet Profile operation: kerf, cut direction, leads, tabs, the waterjet machine and post it needs, and the refusals you are most likely to meet."
+weight = 7
++++
+
+This page is the reference for **Waterjet Profile**, the one kind in the
+**Waterjet** group of the [operations](@/guide/operations/_index.md) ribbon.
+For the tabs themselves and what a click picks, see that page; for what a
+refusal means in general, see [Reading a refusal](@/guide/reference/refusals.md).
+
+Lengths are in mm (inches in an inch document), feeds in mm/min (in/min),
+times in seconds.
+
+Blue shows the operation travel; dashed orange shows approach and retract; gray shows the workpiece. These schematics are not generated NC paths and have no scale.
+
+## The machine, the tool and the post
+
+**A waterjet machine.** Waterjet Profile needs a setup whose machine is a
+waterjet (see [Machines](@/guide/check-and-post/machines.md)).
+
+**A nozzle.** The tool is a **Waterjet nozzle**, and its diameter is the
+kerf width. Another tool kind is refused ("a waterjet profile mounts a
+waterjet nozzle, not a ... - its diameter is the kerf width").
+
+**A waterjet post.** The generic ISO abrasive waterjet post
+(`waterjet-iso.cps`) serves waterjet machines only. It opens and closes
+the jet for each contour, and it can send arcs as straight lines for a
+control without G2/G3. When a post without the jet hooks meets a
+waterjet section, the post warnings name it ("... does not define onJetOn
+/ onJetOff - use a waterjet post").
+
+## Waterjet Profile
+
+{{ <icon name="op-waterjet-profile" /> }} ![Top view of jet travel from a pierce point in the scrap along an arc lead and around the outer sheet profile.](../../../operation-paths.svg#WaterjetProfile)
+
+**For:** cutting parts out of flat sheet: one through-cut per contour,
+with the kerf offset to the waste side, leads that start in the scrap,
+and holes cut before the outline that frees the part.
+
+**Picks:** the closed contours and open runs to cut, on the Geometry tab.
+Without picks it cuts the through-silhouette of the model.
+
+| Tab | Setting | Default |
+|---|---|---|
+| Geometry | Kerf width | Nozzle: the nozzle's diameter |
+| Geometry | Compensation | In computer (offset path); or In control (G41/G42) |
+| Geometry | Direction | Outer CW, holes CCW; or Reversed: outer CCW, holes CW |
+| Geometry | Open run side | On the centre line |
+| Geometry | Send arcs as lines | off (line tolerance 0.01 when on) |
+| Heights | Clearance (jet off) / Top of sheet / Bottom of sheet | from the setup |
+| Passes | Hold with tabs | off |
+| Lead in / Lead out | Lead shape | Arc |
+| Lead in / Lead out | Lead-in length / Lead-out length | 3 / 2 |
+| Feeds | Cut feed | 100 |
+| Feeds | Pierce time / Abrasive delay | 1 / 0 |
+
+**Kerf.** The path is the jet centre: each cutting move stands half the
+kerf off the part on the waste side. One through-cut is made at the sheet
+top; there are no depth steps.
+
+**Leads.** The pierce is made in the scrap. A lead with no room beside
+the part is shortened, and a tight hole is pierced at its centre.
+
+**Feeds.** State the cut data for the material and the sheet thickness
+from the nozzle's recipe. The default feed and pierce time are only a
+safe start.
+
+**Common refusals:** "waterjet profile: no contour to cut"; "waterjet
+profile: the sheet's bottom (...) stands above its top (...)"; "the kerf
+width must be a positive number (it is ...)"; "the cut feed must be a
+positive number (it is ...)".

+## Upgrade to 0.26.0
+
+CamCraft 0.26.0 saves project format **78**. It opens supported older
+projects and converts them on load. Older builds, including 0.25.0, refuse a project
+saved by 0.26.0. Keep an older copy if another person still needs an older
+build. This format change includes the Deburr chord-width meaning,
+setup creation order and stored tool reservations.
+
+Generate each **part-off** operation again before posting an older
+project. The kerf now lies entirely on the bar side of the parting plane;
+an earlier cached path cannot post until it is regenerated
+([#3452](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3452)).
+
+For a **STEP** file with no length unit, the desktop app asks whether the
+model was drawn in **millimetres** or **inches**. Choose the intended
+unit; Cancel imports nothing. CamCraft no longer assumes millimetres.
+MCP and script imports must state `units` (`"mm"` or `"in"`). See
+[Units and coordinates](@/guide/reference/units-and-coordinates.md#imported-models)
+for the existing unit rules and the limits for holders and fixtures.

+## Typed text as outline shapes
+
+Outline text makes closed letter shapes in a **TrueType** font. It is
+different from the single-line strokes used for engraving text. A letter's
+inner loop, such as the hole in O, stays a hole. The shapes are stored in
+the project as a profile on the setup's stock top; the font is not needed
+to reopen that profile.
+
+In 0.26.0 there is no desktop outline-font dialog or font picker. Create
+the stock first, then use an [MCP agent](@/guide/automate/mcp.md) connected
+to the app to call `insert_outline_text`. For example, the tool arguments
+below place the left end of the baseline 10 mm across and 5 mm along the
+stock top from its origin. Replace the font path with a file on the
+computer running CamCraft:
+
+```json
+{
+  "font": "/path/to/font.ttf",
+  "text": "PART 01",
+  "height": 7,
+  "position": [10, 5],
+  "angle": 0,
+  "letter_spacing": 0,
+  "name": "Part label"
+}
+```
+
+`height` is the font's cap height in mm, from 0.5 to 1000. `angle` turns
+the baseline counterclockwise in degrees when seen from above.
+`letter_spacing` adds a gap in mm between letters. Use a `.ttf` file or
+an `.otf` file with TrueType outlines. CFF outlines, font collections,
+missing characters, crossing or touching outlines, and empty text are
+refused by name. The setup must have stock.
+
+The result appears with the other **DXF profiles** on the Stock page.
+Use **Profile X**, **Profile Y**, **Profile angle (deg)** and
+**Place profile** to move it as described above. Insertion is one undo
+step. Saving the project keeps the closed shapes. The current profile
+generation limit above also applies to outline text: an operation can
+name it as its source, but generation from its chains is not available
+in this release. It does not produce a machinable text toolpath yet.
+

+"""Provenance: released CamCraft 0.26.0 assets and documentation gaps in #3769."""
+
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import unittest
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+GUIDE = ROOT / "site/content/guide"
+
+# Freeze the release inventory: the same guide changes also go to main.
+POSTS_026 = (
+    "agie-native", "carvera", "doosan-dnm", "fanuc", "fanuc-lathe",
+    "g-edm", "grbl", "grblhal", "haas", "heidenhain",
+    "heidenhain-klartext", "linuxcnc", "mach3", "mach4", "mazak",
+    "richauto", "sinker-iso", "sinumerik", "sinumerik-810m", "sodick-wire",
+    "tinyg", "tormach", "tormach-lathe", "tormach-plasma", "waterjet-iso",
+    "wire-iso",
+)
+MACHINES_026 = (
+    "3axis-vmc", "agiecut-classic-2s", "doosan-dnm", "doosan-dnm-3axis",
+    "emco-vmc-200", "fehlmann-picomax55", "grbl-3axis", "grblhal-3axis",
+    "haas-dm1", "haas-dt1", "haas-mini-mill", "haas-vf2", "haas-vf2ss",
+    "lathe", "linuxcnc-3axis", "makera-carvera", "makera-carvera-air",
+    "makera-z1", "millturn", "ooznest-workbee-1000x1500", "sienci-altmill-2x4",
+    "sienci-altmill-4x4", "sienci-altmill-4x8", "sinker-edm", "sodick-alc400g",
+    "tilthead", "tinyg-3axis", "tormach-1100m", "tormach-1100m-plus",
+    "tormach-1100mx", "tormach-1300pl", "tormach-1500mx",
+    "tormach-15l-slant-pro", "tormach-15lx-slant-pro", "tormach-24r",
+    "tormach-770m", "tormach-770m-plus", "tormach-770mx",
+    "tormach-770mx-microarc4", "tormach-770mx-ml", "tormach-8l",
+    "tormach-pcnc1100-s1", "tormach-pcnc1100-s2", "tormach-pcnc1100-s3",
+    "tormach-pcnc440", "tormach-pcnc770", "tormach-pcnc770-s3",
+    "tormach-xstech", "tormach-xstech-pro", "vmc",
+)
+
+
+def page(path):
+    return " ".join((GUIDE / path).read_text().lower().split())
+
+
+def section(path, heading):
+    source = (GUIDE / path).read_text()
+    parts = re.split(r"^## (.+)$", source, flags=re.M)
+    sections = dict(zip(parts[1::2], parts[2::2]))
+    return " ".join(sections[heading].lower().split())
+
+
+class Release026Gaps(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_post_inventory_names_each_shipped_script_and_control(self):
+        source = (GUIDE / "check-and-post/posting.md").read_text()
+        rows = [line.lower() for line in source.splitlines() if line.startswith("|")]
+        for stem in POSTS_026:
+            with self.subTest(post=stem):
+                matches = [row for row in rows if f"`{stem}.cps`" in row]
+                self.assertEqual(len(matches), 1, f"Add one inventory row for {stem}.cps")
+                self.assertGreaterEqual(len(matches[0].split("|")), 5)
+        for stem in MACHINES_026:
+            with self.subTest(machine=stem):
+                self.assertIn(f"`{stem}.mch`", source)
+        for filename, facts in (
+            ("mach3.cps", ("mach3", "mill")),
+            ("sinumerik-810m.cps", ("810m", "emco-vmc-200.mch")),
+            ("agie-native.cps", ("agie", "agiecut-classic-2s.mch")),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(post=filename):
+                row = next((row for row in rows if f"`{filename}`" in row), "")
+                for fact in facts:
+                    self.assertIn(fact, row)
+
+    def test_do_not_touch_is_documented_on_each_added_operation(self):
+        for path, heading in (
+            ("operations/operations-2d.md", "Face"),
+            ("operations/operations-2d.md", "Trace"),
+            ("operations/operations-2d.md", "Engrave"),
+            ("operations/operations-2d.md", "2D Adaptive"),
+            ("operations/operations-3d.md", "3D Finish"),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(operation=heading):
+                text = section(path, heading)
+                self.assertIn("do not touch", text)
+                self.assertRegex(text, r"(boundar|geometry)")
+                self.assertRegex(text, r"(protect|keep.out|clearance)")
+
+    def test_outline_text_explains_creation_and_profile_use(self):
+        text = page("set-up/setups.md")
+        for fact in ("insert_outline_text", "truetype", '"font"', '"height"',
+                     "stock", "profile", "undo"):
+            with self.subTest(fact=fact):
+                self.assertIn(fact, text)
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"(no|not|without).{0,80}(dialog|font picker)")
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"(shapes|outlines).{0,100}(sav|stor)")
+        self.assertIn("@/guide/automate/mcp.md", text)
+
+    def test_offset_warns_about_released_inside_outside_paths(self):
+        text = section("operations/operations-2d.md", "2D Offset")
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"known.{0,15}issue")
+        for fact in ("0.26.0", "inside", "outside", "ramp", "lift"):
+            with self.subTest(fact=fact):
+                self.assertIn(fact, text)
+        for number in (3741, 3744, 3745, 3746, 3747, 3748):
+            with self.subTest(issue=number):
+                self.assertIn(f"https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/{number}".lower(), text)
+
+    def test_upgrade_notes_cover_format_regeneration_and_unit_question(self):
+        text = page("reference/migrating.md")
+        self.assertIn("0.26.0", text)
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"format.{0,30}78")
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"older.{0,80}refus")
+        self.assertIn("part-off", text)
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"(regenerat|generate.{0,20}again)")
+        self.assertIn("https://github.com/neotech/camcraft/issues/3452", text)
+        for fact in ("step", "millimet", "inch", "@/guide/reference/units-and-coordinates.md"):
+            with self.subTest(fact=fact):
+                self.assertIn(fact, text)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
